Compute and Store the Bootstrap Replicates of a Fit

Source: R/bootstrap_fit.R
add_bootstrap.Rd

Refits the model on resampled data sets and stores the coefficients of the replicates in the fit. The replicates are read by bootstrap_vcov() and returned by statmod_bootstrap().

Usage

add_bootstrap(
  fit,
  n = 200L,
  resample = parametric_resample(),
  refit = c("coefficients", "full"),
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

n

A single whole number, the total number of replicates wanted.

resample

A resample_method object: parametric_resample() (the default), case_resample(), cluster_resample() or bayesian_resample().

refit

"coefficients" (the default) re-estimates the coefficients at the hyperparameters of the fit, and "full" selects the hyperparameters again on every replicate.

cores

The number of separate R processes over which the refits are distributed, a single whole number (default 1, no process besides this one). It is distinct from the threads of statmod(), which counts threads inside one process; a refit that runs in a separate process is sequential.

Value

fit, invisibly.

Details

The fit keeps a collection of entries, one for each combination of resample and refit. A call with a combination that is not in the collection adds an entry, and a call never overwrites one. The collection is kept in an environment that belongs to the fit object, so the function changes the object in place and returns it, and a copy of the fit made with S7::set_props() shares the environment. An entry is used only by a fit with the coefficients and hyperparameters that it was computed for.

n is the total number of replicates that is wanted. If the entry holds \(m\) replicates, \(n > m\) computes the \(n - m\) missing ones, \(n = m\) computes nothing, and \(n < m\) computes nothing and leaves the \(m\) stored (the first \(n\) are the ones that bootstrap_vcov() uses). Repeating a call does not change the result.

The draws come from the random number stream of the session, one replicate after another in the calling process, and the refits are distributed over cores separate R processes. The result therefore depends on the state of .Random.seed at the call, and not on cores. The state at the start of the stream and after the last replicate kept is stored in the entry, and an extension continues from the second: 500 replicates and then 300 more equal the 800 replicates of a single call from the same seed. After the call .Random.seed is the state after the last replicate kept.

A replicate that fails (an error in the refit, a mode error above mode_error_limit(), or a coefficient that is not identified in the replicate and is in the fit) is replaced by the next draw of the stream. The entry records the failures by cause. The function stops with an error when the failures outnumber the successes after ten draws. Replacing a failed replicate conditions the bootstrap on success, so it understates the variability when failures are frequent.

The refits use the inner_information of the fit. A fit with a response that is not one number per observation, or (with refit = "full") a cv() criterion is rejected, and so are case_resample() and bayesian_resample() beside a modelterms7::random() term.

A fit with a score-driven or a regime term (modelterms7::gas(), modelterms7::regime()) takes parametric_resample() only. Each replicate is a new path of the series, drawn through modelterms7::term_simulate() at the fitted coefficients and parameters of the term, so the recursion of the filter runs on the draws; it is not the fitted filtered path with new noise. A resample of rows or of groups breaks the recursion at every join, and case_resample(), cluster_resample() and bayesian_resample() signal an error that names parametric_resample(). The effects of a modelterms7::random() term keep their estimates in the draws. The replicates hold the free parameters of the term after the coefficients, on the unconstrained scale, in the order of vcov(). A replicate is kept when the Newton decrement of the refit over the coefficients and the term's parameters is below mode_error_limit() (a score-driven term), or when the refit is finite (a regime term).

A fit with a break-point term (modelterms7::seg(), modelterms7::jump(), modelterms7::jseg()) or a nonlinear term (modelterms7::nl()) is refitted on every replicate from the break-points and coefficients of the fit, and the refit then runs the restart cycle of statmod() (bootstrap restarting with the budget n_boot of the terms, and the settling of the sharp break-points), because a refit that stopped at the local optimum nearest to the fit's positions would be another estimator. A position is a coefficient of the term, so its variance is that of the replicates. The slot of a sharp modelterms7::jump() or modelterms7::jseg(), which the fit holds at a working value, stores the position of the break-point in the replicates. The generator of the restart cycle is seeded from the draw of the replicate, so the result does not depend on cores. A replicate is kept when its coefficients are finite.

See also

statmod_bootstrap() to read the entries, bootstrap_vcov() for the variance, and resample_method for the schemes.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)

set.seed(2)
fit <- add_bootstrap(fit, n = 20, resample = case_resample())
# extend the entry to 30 replicates: only the last 10 are computed
fit <- add_bootstrap(fit, n = 30, resample = case_resample())
statmod_bootstrap(fit)
#>   resample        refit replicates replaced error mode_error unidentified
#> 1     case coefficients         30        0     0          0            0
